turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning, I'm just going to pop these numbers down before the doctor comes. Blood pressure is 132 over 84, pulse 78, temperature 36.7, and your oxygen is 98 percent.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay shame, thank you sister. I hope the pressure isn't hectic, I rushed from the robot by the mall and I was a bit flustered. Anyway that's not why I'm here.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come in, have a seat. I've had a look at the vitals sister took, all fine. What's brought you in today?

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): It's this pain, doctor, up here on the right side of my stomach, just under the ribs. It comes after I eat fatty things, like if we braai and I have boerewors and slap chips, and then it sits there for hours. I nearly didn't come, I thought ag it'll pass, but it keeps coming back.
[SEG0005] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ja, and it's been going on a good month now. Every time she eats anything rich she ends up throwing up, I've watched it.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag no, Sibu, that's not right. It's been about two weeks, not a month, and I only vomited that one time, after the braai at your brother's, not every single time.

[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): Okay, so I'm hearing two versions on the timing. Somewhere between two weeks and a month, and you two don't agree on the vomiting. Let me park that and get your story properly.

[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): So the pain, umm, whether it's two weeks or his month, it starts maybe an hour after the fatty meal, on the right, and it can go on for three hours, sometimes four. I can't get comfortable, I just walk around the lounge. The one night I did vomit, just once, and then the pain carried on a bit and faded.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right. Any fever with it? Yellow eyes, dark urine, pale stools?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever, no. And my eyes aren't yellow, he would have told me, he notices everything. Urine looks normal and the stools are a normal colour, just ordinary.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the bowels themselves, any diarrhoea or constipation?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No diarrhoea. I go every morning like clockwork, I have since I was a girl, same time after coffee. No change there.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Chest pain, shortness of breath, anything in the breathing?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No, chest is fine, breathing is fine. I even walked up the stairs at work yesterday, I'm an admin clerk at the municipality, and I was okay apart from the tummy.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Waterworks, any burning or going more often?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that. Completely normal, same as always.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any headaches, dizziness, funny turns, that neurological side?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that at all.
[SEG0019] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She also gets this burning though, and she lives on that antacid from the chemist.

[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, I was getting to that. I take gavascon, the mint liquid. I thought it was two spoons but the little cup says 10 ml, so it's 10 ml after a fatty supper. The bottle actually says twice a day and at bedtime, but I only do it when I've had the rich food, so I'm not really taking it the way it says.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Gaviscon 10 ml after the fatty meals, not the full label schedule. That's useful. Anything else, pain tablets?

[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Panado, when the pain is really going. Two of the 500 milligram ones, so a gram, maybe three times in these past weeks. It takes the edge off a little, not completely, and the gavascon helps the burn more than the actual pain.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Allergies to medicines? Anything that breaks you out or swells you up?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing. I've never reacted to a medicine.
[SEG0025] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): What about the penicillin, when you got that rash as a kid? You always say they told your mother to avoid it.

[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): That was my sister Lindi, not me. People mix us up our whole lives, even at family braais. I have taken penicillin, whatever the dentist gave me years ago, and I was fine. No allergies.

[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Alright. I'll note that you say no allergies, and your husband thinks there was a penicillin rash, so that one's not settled. We're not needing an antibiotic today anyway.

[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): And my mother, I should say, she had her gallbladder out, umm, about ten years ago in Durban. Same kind of pain, she told me, after fatty food, and they found stones. That's why I got a bit scared, I kept thinking about her the whole drive here.

[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Family history matters here, ja. Gallbladder trouble does run in families sometimes. This pattern, right upper pain after fat, lasting hours, sounds like biliary colic, gallstones possibly, but I can't say that for sure till we look.

[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): They did check my blood once, I should mention. At the day hospital they said my cholesterol was borderline, but I never saw the actual number. And I can't remember if that was last year or the year before, err, the lady just said borderline and to watch the braai.

[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): So an old cholesterol test, told to you as borderline, no figure, and the date is fuzzy. I won't treat that as a real result, we'll do fresh bloods. Let me have a feel of your tummy first.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Tummy is soft. There's tenderness under the right ribs when I press, and no guarding. Murphy's sign is positive on that side. Bowel sounds are normal.

[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja that's the spot, that's exactly where it grabs me. It goes through a bit to the back sometimes, but not always, I don't want to overstate it. If I lie on my left it doesn't really help, I just wait it out.

[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Through to the back sometimes, noted. I wouldn't fully rule out a stomach ulcer either, given the burning, but the fatty-meal pattern pulls me toward the gallbladder. Working idea, not a diagnosis.

[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): So the plan. Sister will take your bloods Thursday morning, liver tests and a lipase, and you must fast from midnight, just water. I'm also booking the abdominal ultrasound for Tuesday morning, nothing to eat for six hours before that. Those two are booked, they're happening.

[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): If those liver tests come back borderline, then we do an MRCP, a bile duct scan, as a third test, and if they're not borderline we don't. I'll see you back here in two weeks with the results. Mm, that's the shape of it.

[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Thursday bloods fasting, and Tuesday the scan, also fasting. And only if the bloods are borderline, the other scan. Should I still take the gavascon before the bloods, because some mornings the burn is there even before I eat, especially if supper was heavy?

[SEG0038] person_1 (NURSE): Don't take the gavascon on Thursday morning, only after the bloods if you need it. Fast from midnight, water is fine, and come at half past seven, I'll put you in the book. The ultrasound fasting is six hours, and the radiology clerk will sms you the Tuesday time.

[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ja. Lay off the boerewors and the vetkoek for now, low fat, and keep the gaviscon at 10 ml when the burn comes. If the pain gets savage, or you start vomiting again, or you go yellow, don't wait for the two weeks, come straight in. Otherwise I'll see you in two weeks. Sharp.

spec.situation: Woman with right-upper stomach pain after fatty meals, lasting hours, once with vomiting; takes antacid; mother had gallbladder surgery; blood tests and ultrasound planned.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.

omissions.text: Right upper abdominal pain is associated with inability to get comfortable/walking around during attacks, and lying on the left does not help.
Pain radiates through to the back only sometimes, not always.
Vomiting occurred once after a braai and the pain continued for a while before fading.
Panado/paracetamol was taken as two 500 mg tablets (1 g) only about three times over the past weeks; it only takes the edge off and does not completely relieve the pain.
Gaviscon helps the burning more than the actual abdominal pain.
The patient also reports burning/heartburn sometimes even before eating in the morning, especially if supper was heavy.
No headaches, dizziness, or funny turns was asked and answered, but the recorded review of systems missed that this was a direct doctor ROS question with current negatives.
Old cholesterol result was specifically described as 'borderline' by the patient, but the doctor said he would not treat it as a real result and would repeat fresh bloods.
The abdominal ultrasound timing is not actually fixed as 'Tuesday morning' in the final instructions; the radiology clerk will SMS the Tuesday time, with six hours fasting beforehand.

findings.detail: allergy 'penicillin' is recorded, but the conversation cited for it reads like a denial ('That was my sister Lindi, not me. People mix us up our whole lives, even at fami'); confirm with the patient; clinician review required
